name: Bastard Children
overview: The Bible addresses the status and spiritual implications of those referred to as 'bastards' with a focus on their exclusion from the congregation of the Lord, as seen in Deuteronomy 23:2, where such individuals are barred even to the tenth generation. The example of Jephthah, born of a harlot (Judges 11:1), demonstrates that God can use those with difficult beginnings for His purposes. Zechariah 9:6 speaks of a bastard dwelling in Ashdod, indicating God's sovereign control over all peoples. Hebrews 12:8 contrasts true sons with 'bastards,' emphasizing that discipline from God marks genuine sonship. Ultimately, John 3:16 reminds us that God’s love and the gift of His only begotten Son offer a path to true belonging and eternal life, transcending earthly status.
